# Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects

## Problem statement

The generalised storyline option model (`StorylineOption`) currently supports
only a label, a single successor, and an apply/skip effect policy. Content and
engine authors cannot express options that are only available when the player
can afford them, that branch to different successors based on game state, or
that carry their own extra effects. The game-agnostic seam
(`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) was explicitly designed to grow into these
semantics, and this capability was deliberately deferred from the
`write-storylines` epic as speculative until now.

## Users

- **Engine/content authors** — need richer per-option semantics (affordability
  gates, state-based branching, extra effects) without bypassing the
  game-agnostic seam or hand-writing bespoke engine code per card.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need the extension to stay declarative,
  serialisable, statically validatable, and portable to the core engine.
- **Players** — should only be offered choices they can actually take, and
  should have their decisions reflected accurately in coins/reputation.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — must keep selecting legal, presented options so
  headless games never stall or pick a hidden/unaffordable branch.

### Example user stories

- "As an engine author, I want to gate an option behind a coin/reputation cost,
  so the choice only appears when the player can afford it."
- "As a content designer, I want an option's successor to depend on coins or
  reputation, so one choice can lead down different branches."
- "As a content designer, I want an option to apply an extra effect on top of
  its apply/skip policy, so choices can have their own consequences."
- "As a developer, I want invalid cost/condition data to fail the validator, so
  mis-authored storylines cannot ship."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Backwards-compatible model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional `cost`, `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors` fields; all three optional, omitting preserves current behaviour.
- **Cost gating.** Options whose `cost.coins` exceeds `state.resourceBank.coins`, or whose `cost.reputation` exceeds `state.resourceBank.reputation`, are omitted from the presented list; options with no cost always included.
- **Presented list stability.** `PendingEventChoice.options` stores the draw-time snapshot populated at choice draw time; the presented list is computed once at draw and is stable.
- **Cost deduction.** Selecting an affordable option deducts cost coins and cost reputation from `state.resourceBank`.
- **Extra effects.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`; both can coexist.
- **Loss checks and logging.** If deduction drops coins or reputation to zero, normal loss checks fire; activity log reflects cost deduction and extra effects.
- **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule matching `state.resourceBank` field determines the pushed card ID; `successorId` fallback when no conditions match.
- **Boundary coverage.** All boundary cases tested: above/below threshold, equality boundary, and no-match fallback; matched successor pushed via `pushChainCard`.
- **Precedence.** `successorResolver` wins when present; otherwise conditional rules run before `successorIds` random draw and legacy `successorId`; a matching rule consumes no RNG draw.
- **AI selection.** The AI considers only options in the presented list; when a pending choice exists it reads the frozen pending snapshot, otherwise the state-filtered list.
- **Cost-aware scoring.** Projected option value subtracts `cost.coins` and `cost.reputation` and adds `extraEffect` before comparing options.
- **AI harnesses.** Monte Carlo and regression harnesses run to completion without AI stalls or invalid selections; legacy binary-choice AI behaviour identical.
- **Static validation.** Reject negative or zero costs; reject conditions with unknown field or op; reject non-numeric value; reject negative extra effect values; reject dangling conditional successors.
- **Schema and shipped content.** Shipped content validates cleanly: all shipped CSVs produce valid storylines; JSON schema accepts the new optional fields; doc-drift test passes.
- **Documentation.** `docs/game/storylines.md` documents the extended `StorylineOption` fields `cost`, `extraEffect`, `conditionalSuccessors` with examples; resolution lifecycle documented.
- **Seam, CSV and roadmap docs.** `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` migration notes updated; `src/README.md` confirms the new semantics are programmatic via `registerStorylineOptions`, not CSV-authored; roadmap updated.

## Constraints

- **Programmatic authoring only for the new semantics (producer decision
  Q1=A).** Extend the in-memory model, engine resolution, validator, and
  schema. The CSV `options` column now authors arbitrary labels/candidate sets
  (MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144), but it must **not** gain cost, extra-effect, or
  conditional-column authoring in this work; those stay programmatic via
  `registerStorylineOptions`.
- **Declarative and serialisable (producer decision Q3=A).** Only
  field/op/value conditions and numeric deltas. Arbitrary callbacks are out of
  scope here — see the follow-up work item below.
- **Game-agnostic seam.** New semantics must live behind
  `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` and keep the future core-engine extraction
  viable (pure/declarative data, no Main-Street globals baked in beyond the
  injected template registry).
- **Affordability is coins and/or reputation (producer decision Q2.1).** A cost
  may specify either or both; an option is available only when *all* specified
  costs are affordable.
- **Omit, do not disable (producer decision Q2.2).** Unaffordable options are
  removed from the presented list, not shown greyed out.
- **Cost is a real payment (producer decision Q2.3).** Deducted from the
  player in addition to the option's apply/skip effect policy.
- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  gameplay must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- **Full suite gate (delivery gate, not a child feature).** Every child's
  definition of done includes a green full project test suite; the epic is not
  complete until the full suite passes with zero behavioural deltas for
  existing content.

## Existing state (verified against the codebase on this plan revision)

- `StorylineOption` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) has since grown beyond the
  original three-field shape: `{ label, successorId? (deprecated), successorIds?
  (random candidate set), effectPolicy, condition? (draw-time callback),
  successorResolver? (resolution-time callback) }`. `CompiledStoryline` wraps
  an ordered option list.
- CSV authoring was generalised by MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144: the `options` column
  decodes to arbitrary labelled options with candidate successor sets
  (`parseStorylineOptionsEncoding`), not just two-way Accept/Reject.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice(event, state)` (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`)
  already freezes a draw-time, condition-filtered snapshot onto
  `PendingEventChoice.options`; `getPendingStorylineOptions(pending, state)`
  reads it (with a recompile fallback), and `resolveEventOption`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) already indexes that snapshot and
  records the option label as the transcript token.
- `resolveStorylineOption(state, event, option)` applies `effectPolicy` and
  resolves the successor with documented precedence: `successorResolver` →
  `successorIds` (one seeded RNG draw) → legacy `successorId`.
- `decideEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`) already returns an
  option **index** (not binary accept/reject) and picks the option with the
  lowest pessimistic successor severity, but it calls
  `getStorylineOptions(event)` without state and ignores cost/extra effects.
- Validation lives in `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`; the manifest/schema
  in `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`; the canonical docs are
  `docs/game/storylines.md` (§2 model, §3 lifecycle, §9 seam, §10 roadmap),
  `src/README.md`, and `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md`.
- None of `cost`, `extraEffect`, or declarative `conditionalSuccessors` exists
  anywhere in `src/` today — those are the genuine remaining gaps.

## Desired change

Extend the **current** option model and resolution path (which already has
callback conditions, callbacks resolvers, random candidate sets, and a frozen
draw-time snapshot) so that:

1. Options declare an optional declarative affordability `cost`; the
   draw-time presented list (already snapshotted on `PendingEventChoice.options`)
   additionally filters out unaffordable options.
2. Options declare an optional `extraEffect` and ordered declarative
   `conditionalSuccessors`, both applied/selected at resolution time.
3. Selection applies the `effectPolicy` effect (unchanged), deducts `cost`,
   applies `extraEffect` independently, and pushes the resolver-precedence
   successor, honouring the declarative rules.
4. The validator, schema, and graph/manifest export understand the new fields;
   the AI policy operates over the presented snapshot and accounts for
   cost/extra-effect deltas.

## Plan revision note (this planning session)

Three of the eight children created by the previous plan run were written
against a superseded code shape. Revision outcome:

- **Closed as already implemented:** "Update engine turn closing to use
  presented option list" — `resolveEventOption` already indexes the frozen
  `pending.options` snapshot with a recompile fallback and label-based
  transcripts (shipped by F3, `MS-0MV8KQL820077BOS`).
- **Rewritten to the remaining gap:** "Add affordability filtering" now covers
  only cost-based filtering on top of the existing snapshot; "AI
  cost-awareness" now targets the existing index-returning `decideEventChoice`;
  "model extension" and "validator/schema" now extend the current field set;
  "documentation" now targets `docs/game/storylines.md`.
- Dependency order is unchanged; test coverage stays embedded per feature
  (TDD within each child) plus the existing regression/Monte Carlo harness.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — Extend `StorylineOption` with `cost`,
  `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors`; add a `Condition` type.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Add cost filtering to the existing draw-time
  snapshot path, apply cost + extra effects in `resolveStorylineOption`,
  resolve declarative conditional successors by the documented precedence.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PendingEventChoice.options` snapshot already
  exists; document that it now carries cost-filtered lists (no new field).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Update cost/extra-effect logging and
  totals in `resolveEventOption` (snapshot indexing is already implemented).
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` selects only among
  presented options and accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — Validate cost/extra-effect/condition
  data and conditional successor targets.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`
  — Represent and validate the new option metadata in the manifest/graph.
- `docs/game/storylines.md`, `src/README.md`,
  `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` — Document the extended option
  model, resolution semantics, and programmatic-only authoring.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storyline-regression-harness.test.ts` — New/extended
  coverage.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV` — **write storylines** (completed epic; parent context).
- `MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV` — **Storyline model & extraction seam** (completed; the
  generalised `StorylineOption` this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP92O9002772U` — **Storyline behaviour regression harness** (completed;
  the byte-for-byte regression guard).
- `MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6` — **Static validator & npm gate** (completed; the
  validator this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ` — **Storyline authoring helper CLI** (completed).
- `MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0` — **Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema**
  (completed; manifest/schema this extends).
- `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N` — **Support arbitrary callback conditions/successors in
  storyline options** (follow-up, medium priority, `discovered-from` this item).
- Roadmap entry: `docs/game/storylines.md` §10.

## Risks

- **Cost filtering changes the index space.** The draw-time snapshot
  (`PendingEventChoice.options`) already freezes the presented list, so cost
  filtering inherits that stability — but the AI must read the snapshot (not
  recompile) or it will disagree with the UI and transcript. *Mitigation:*
  `decideEventChoice` reads `getPendingStorylineOptions` and is covered by
  regression/Monte Carlo tests.
- **AI divergence.** `decideEventChoice` already returns an index, but it
  compiles options without state and ignores cost/extra effects; an option that
  is unaffordable in the snapshot must never be scored or chosen.
  *Mitigation:* score only the presented list and include cost/extra deltas;
  cover with regression/Monte Carlo tests.
- **Precedence ambiguity.** Two successor mechanisms now coexist (callback
  resolver, random candidate set) plus the new declarative rules.
  *Mitigation:* precedence is documented in code and tests (callback >
  declarative rules > random candidates > single successor).
- **Manifest/schema churn.** Adding optional fields can break the graph export
  or doc-drift test. *Mitigation:* keep new fields optional and update schema,
  exporter, and docs in the same change.
- **Scope creep.** Callback conditions/resolvers and CSV label authoring have
  already shipped elsewhere (`MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`, `MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144`); this
  work adds only the declarative cost/extra-effect/conditional-successor fields.
  Per-option animation and CSV cost columns remain out of scope.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface.** How far should this change reach?
  - Answer (producer): **A** — extend the in-memory model + engine resolution +
    validator/schema only, programmatically via `registerStorylineOptions`;
    keep the legacy CSV at two-way Accept/Reject. Source: interactive reply.
    *Note (plan revision 2026-10-19): the CSV `options` column was later
    generalised to arbitrary labels/candidate sets by `MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144`;
    the intent of Q1=A still holds — the new cost/extra-effect/conditional
    semantics stay programmatic and add no CSV columns.*
- **Q2 — Cost-gated semantics.**
  1. What gates eligibility?
     - Answer (producer): **coins and/or reputation**. Source: interactive reply.
  2. When unaffordable, omitted or shown disabled?
     - Answer (producer): **omitted**. Source: interactive reply.
  3. Is the cost deducted on selection in addition to apply/skip?
     - Answer (producer): **yes**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Conditional successors & per-option extra effects representation.**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — declarative, serialisable data
    (`extraEffect` + ordered `{ when, successorId }` rules with `successorId`
    fallback). Additionally: create a **medium-priority follow-up work item**
    to add arbitrary callbacks. Source: interactive reply. Follow-up created as
    `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

- **Q4 — Plan revision against the current codebase (this session).**
  Three of the eight children were drafted against a superseded model. Answer
  (plan skill, evidence-based): close the already-implemented engine child and
  rewrite the rest to the remaining gaps; no new producer decision needed for
  *what* to build, because Q1–Q3 still hold. Sources: `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`,
  `MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144`, `MS-0MV8KQL820077BOS`.

### Assumptions

- **Resolution order.** The `effectPolicy` effect is applied first (preserving
  today's behaviour exactly), then `cost` is deducted, then `extraEffect` is
  applied; the returned `coinChange`/`repChange` deltas cover all three.
- **Successor precedence.** `successorResolver` callback (existing escape
  hatch) > declarative `conditionalSuccessors` (first match wins) >
  `successorIds` random candidate draw > legacy `successorId`. A matching
  conditional rule consumes no RNG draw.
- **Affordability boundary.** An option is affordable when
  `cost.coins <= state.resourceBank.coins` and
  `cost.reputation <= state.resourceBank.reputation` (equality is affordable);
  unspecified cost components are unconstrained.
- **Draw-time filtering order.** The existing `condition` callback filter runs
  first, then the new cost filter — an option must pass both to be presented.

- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  legacy/card behaviour must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- Because a pending choice blocks all player actions, the set of affordable
  options is stable between draw and resolution; storing the presented list on
  the pending choice makes this explicit and save/load-safe.
- Cost deduction that drops coins or reputation to zero triggers the normal
  loss checks (no special-casing).

# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-10-01, interactive reply): **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**; **Q2 = A (epic, decomposed into vertical slices)**;
**Q3 = A (curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

Storylines can only be authored today by hand-editing `src/card-data.csv` or by
driving the transaction-safe `storyline-author` CLI, and the graph can only be
viewed as a generated Mermaid/JSON artefact. Content designers therefore cannot
*see* the arc they are editing, cannot discover links and dangling targets
visually, and cannot make a guided, validated edit in one place. The seed
roadmap entry (`docs/game/storylines.md` §10) calls for a visual
storyline authoring editor that reads `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`,
renders the graph interactively, and writes edits back through the same
transactional, self-validating author operations.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — see a storyline's shape at a glance,
  inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename, retarget a
  link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV internals.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — trust that every edit goes through one
  validated, transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync
  with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write
  a dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool that is excluded
  from the game build and reuses the existing author API, so it adds no runtime
  dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

1. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain (no new runtime
   dependency). It is a development tool and must not be included in the game
   build.
2. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and
   node selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

3. A Node-side bridge that exposes the existing author operations
   (`add-card`, `link`, `set-storyline` from `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`)
   and the validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) to the editor.
4. Every edit is **previewed and validated before writing**; an invalid result
   leaves `src/card-data.csv` untouched and surfaces actionable errors.
5. On an accepted edit, regenerate `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd` and
   `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` via the existing
   `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` generator so the existing drift test stays
   green.
6. Concurrency guard: refuse to overwrite the CSV if it changed on disk outside
   the editor session (content hash / mtime check) and ask the author to reload.

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

7. Edit an existing card's fields: name, effect text, coin/reputation deltas,
   `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, `storylineId`,
   `storylineTitle`.
8. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
   pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

9. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
   group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
10. Documentation in `docs/game/storylines.md` (and the `src/README.md`
    script/column references) covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow,
    validation and artefact regeneration.
11. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test
    for the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor` starts the tool
   from the repo root on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain with no new
   runtime dependency; the command is documented in `docs/game/storylines.md`.
   Verified by a test that invokes the entry point (dry/`--help` mode) and asserts
   it exits 0.
2. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the committed
   manifest (`docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`): all nodes and edges
   appear, choice cards are visually distinct, storyline grouping and cycle
   edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its links/metadata. Covered by a
   browser test.
3. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the committed manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and the JSON
   schema.
4. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields
   listed in Scope C and add a card; every mutation is routed through
   `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (`add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`). A test
   asserts no editor module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through that
   module, and a round-trip test proves an edited fixture validates.
5. **Preview and validate-before-write** — every edit shows a preview/diff and
   runs the validator before writing; an invalid edit exits non-zero, writes
   nothing, and surfaces the offending card/link. Covered by unit tests against
   valid and deliberately broken edits.
6. **Artefacts regenerated on accepted edit** — after an accepted edit the tool
   regenerates `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`,
   `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` and the generated per-storyline
   docs/SVGs (`npm run storylines:graph:svg`); `npm run storylines:graph --
   --format json --check`, `npm run storylines:graph:svg -- --check` and
   `tests/main-street/storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` pass. Edits that touch a
   hand-written documented row surface an explicit "manual documentation update
   required" result naming the doc-drift check. Covered by tests.
7. **Concurrency guard** — if `src/card-data.csv` changed on disk since load,
   the editor refuses to write and instructs the author to reload. Covered by a
   unit test.
8. **Game build excluded** — the editor assets/entry are not part of the
   production game bundle; verified by a build/test assertion (e.g. the editor
   entry is not referenced from the game `index.html`/`main.ts` graph).
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `src/README.md`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single write path** — the editor must reuse the existing transactional,
  self-validating author operations; it must not introduce a second way to edit
  `src/card-data.csv`.
- **No new runtime dependency** — reuse the existing Vite/`vite-node`/Vitest/
  Playwright toolchain.
- **Deterministic artefacts** — the manifest/mmd generators must stay
  timestamp-free; the existing drift test must continue to pass.
- **Development tool, not shipped** — the editor must not be pulled into the
  production game build or the packaged Electron app.
- **Backward compatibility** — CSV schema/column order and legacy
  `hasChoices`/accept/reject semantics must be preserved; the C1 regression
  harness must stay green.
- **Preserve designed tension** — the editor is an authoring tool; it must not
  alter player-facing content semantics or reveal escalation content to
  players.
- **UK English** in all UI copy and documentation.
- **Scope guard** — richer option semantics (conditional/cost-gated effects,
  `MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9`) are out of scope; the editor edits today's two-way
  Accept/Reject CSV model. Record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Manifest + schema** — `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` (generated,
  deterministic, 5 storyline ids, 71 nodes, 15 edges, 1 cycle) and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` (draft-07, `additionalProperties:
  false`).
- **Graph export** — `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` with
  `npm run storylines:graph -- --format mermaid|json` and a `--check` drift
  guard; committed `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`.
- **Transactional author API** — `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (CLI
  `npm run storylines:author`, `add-card`/`link`/`set-storyline`): builds the
  edited CSV in memory, loads it through the typed model and validates **before**
  writing; `--dry-run` and `--csv <path>` supported.
- **Validator** — `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` (`validateStorylines`,
  `formatStorylineReport`), cycles informational, `--fail-on-cycle` opt-in.
- **Model/seam** — `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` (`compileStorylineFromEvent`,
  `getStorylineOptions`, `registerStorylineOptions`, `resolveStorylineOption`,
  `pushChainCard`); CSV authoring keeps the two-way representation.
- **Stack** — Vite + Phaser + Electron; scripts run under `vite-node` because
  the card model imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw` query.
- **Gap** — no interactive editor; the only graph view is the static generated
  Mermaid/JSON plus the per-storyline SVG pages rendered by
  `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` (`npm run storylines:graph:svg`,
  completed in `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`). Nothing can edit through a UI.
- **Reusable pieces for the editor** — `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` exports
  `filterManifestByStoryline`, `nodeLabel`, `briefEventDescription`,
  `describeEventImpact` and `describeChoiceRouting` (per-storyline grouping and
  labels); `src/CsvChecksum.ts` exports `computeCsvChecksum` (CSV change
  detection, already used for card-art regeneration); `validate-storylines.ts`
  exports `formatStorylineReport` / `storylineReportToJson` (report rendering).
  The committed manifest currently holds 5 storylines, 71 nodes, 15 edges and
  1 cycle.

## Desired change

1. **Host a local editor** — `npm run storylines:editor` serves an in-repo dev
   page backed by a small Node-side API bridge over the author/validator/graph
   modules.
2. **Interactive viewer** — render the manifest graph with storyline grouping,
   choice/plain distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom/select.

# Intake Brief: Track Synergy Diversity (G4/HHI) and Placement Dominance Post-Rebalance

## Problem Statement

Lower base incomes after the rebalance mean synergy bonuses represent a larger relative share of business income, making placement quality dominant over base economy. The synergy-diversity metric (G4/HHI) must be computed on the after-state Monte Carlo results to confirm no single synergy type is crowding out the others — a risk flagged in the rebalance intake.

## Users

- **Producer / Balance Team**: Needs a quantitative view of whether the rebalance created unintended synergy-type dominance that could narrow gameplay variety or create dominant strategy patterns.

## Existing State

- `computeSynergyDiversity()` already exists in `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` — it computes the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) of synergy type shares from `finalGrid` data on Monte Carlo run summaries.
- The function returns `{ hhi: number; synergyTypeShares: Record<string, number> }`.
- The function requires `finalGrid` (an array of card IDs representing the street grid at run end) on each run summary.
- `finalGrid` is **not currently captured** in `MonteCarloRunSummary` — the field is never populated.
- Card synergy types are defined per-card in `src/card-data.csv` (column `synergyTypes`), with 6 types: Food, Culture, Commerce, Service, Entertainment, Health.
- 10 of 39 business/community-space cards have multi-type synergy (e.g., 'Food|Culture'); the remaining 29 are single-type.
- The existing unit test (`global-metrics.test.ts`) uses a single `cardId → type` map, mapping each card to exactly one type.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **finalGrid is captured in Monte Carlo run summaries** — each `MonteCarloRunSummary` includes a `finalGrid` field containing the card IDs of non-null slots on the street grid at the end of the run. The field is nullable (backward-compatible).
- **Synergy type map is constructed from card templates** — a `Record<string, string[]>` mapping each card ID to its list of synergy types (from `MainStreetCardsTemplates`). Cards with multiple synergy types count for each type in the HHI computation (multi-type card with types A and B contributes +1 to type A count and +1 to type B count).
- **A balance report script produces G4/HHI per difficulty** — running `npx vite-node src/scripts/balance/synergy-diversity-report.ts --seeds 200 --maxTurns 40 --difficulty Medium --json` produces JSON output with HHI and type share distribution for each difficulty level (Easy, Medium, Hard). Output is also written to a markdown file (`docs/dev/assets/synergy-diversity-report.md`) with a summary table.
- **Dominance is flagged** — any synergy type with share > 40% in any difficulty is highlighted in the report output (stderr and markdown). A warning line is emitted per dominance finding.

## Constraints

- **No engine changes.** This task only adds data capture and reporting; it must not modify game engine rules, synergy formula, or card data.
- **Backward compatibility.** Adding `finalGrid` to `MonteCarloRunSummary` must be optional/nullable so existing code that does not populate it continues to work.
- **Performance.** Adding `finalGrid` capture (a shallow copy of non-null grid entries) per run should add negligible overhead (< 1ms per run).
- **Canonical profile.** The report should default to the canonical profile: 200 seeds, 60 max turns, `greedy` strategy — matching the rebalance evidence baseline. The `--maxTurns` flag should accept override.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Add `finalGrid?: string[]` to `MonteCarloRunSummary`; capture grid state at end of `simulateSeed`; handle competitive runs too.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` — Update `computeSynergyDiversity` to accept `Record<string, string[]>` (array of types per card) and handle multi-type cards.
- `src/scripts/balance/synergy-diversity-report.ts` — New report script (patterned after `competitive-placement-report.ts`).
- `tests/main-street/balance/global-metrics.test.ts` — Update G4 test for multi-type card handling.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-run-summary-extensions.test.ts` — Add test for `finalGrid` capture.

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — Parent work item: Main Street rebalance evaluation.
- **docs/dev/further-balancing-recommendations.md §3 & R5** — Source of this work item. The rebalance analysis flagged synergy distortion as acceptable but needing monitoring.
- **MS-0MUQUBKNE007NYR8** — Parent: Further-balancing-recommendations artefact.
- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** — Related rebalance tuning (reputation sources); completed.
- **MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X** — Generate Mermaid diagrams for card synergies (open, low priority, unrelated).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** Multi-type cards count for each of their synergy types in the HHI denominator. This is the most defensible interpretation: a card occupying a grid slot provides all of its synergy types simultaneously, so each type should get credit.
- **Assumption:** The canonical Monte Carlo profile uses `mc-balance` seed prefix and `GreedyStrategy` for all seats — matching the existing rebalance baseline. If the competitive profile (multi-player) is needed, `finalGrid` must also be captured in competitive runs.
- **Risk:** Capturing `finalGrid` on every run adds memory pressure if runs are not garbage-collected promptly. Mitigation: store only card ID strings (not full card objects), and do the copy inline rather than holding references.
- **Risk:** If `finalGrid` is missing from existing stored run summaries (legacy data), the function degrades gracefully to `null` — no action needed.

# Add cost-based affordability filtering to the draw-time option snapshot

## Summary

`createPendingStorylineChoice(event, state)` already freezes a
condition-filtered option list into `PendingEventChoice.options`. Extend that
draw-time filter so options whose declarative `cost` exceeds the player's
coins/reputation are omitted from the snapshot. No new state field is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost filter.** Options whose `cost.coins` exceeds `state.resourceBank.coins`, or whose `cost.reputation` exceeds `state.resourceBank.reputation`, are omitted from the presented list; options with no cost are always included.
- **Combined filtering.** An option must pass both the existing `condition` callback and the new cost check to be presented; unaffordable options are omitted rather than disabled.
- **Snapshot stability.** Filtering happens once at draw time and the frozen `pending.options` list is what resolution reads; the presented list is computed once at draw and is stable.
- **Backwards compatible.** Events with no cost-gated options return the same list as before, and legacy pending choices without a snapshot still fall back to recompiling.
- **Boundary coverage.** Cost equal to the current balance is affordable; both coins and reputation gates are enforced when both are specified.

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — cost filtering inside `compileStorylineFromEvent` / `createPendingStorylineChoice`.

# Resolve declarative conditional successors at option resolution

## Summary

Evaluate an option's ordered `conditionalSuccessors` rules at resolution time
inside `resolveStorylineOption`, ahead of the existing random candidate draw.
Rules are declarative and serialisable; the callback `successorResolver` keeps
highest precedence as the existing escape hatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule matching `state.resourceBank` field determines the pushed card ID; `successorId` fallback when no conditions match.

- **Null target.** A matching rule with `successorId: null` ends the chain without pushing a card.
- **Boundary coverage.** All boundary cases tested: above/below threshold, equality boundary, and no-match fallback; matched successor pushed via `pushChainCard`.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `conditionalSuccessors` keep today's resolver/random/single-successor behaviour.

**Work item:** MS-0MV035PRV002QDG4 · `task` · `low`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M (Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance)

## Headline

Two expensive-tier level-0 branching upgrades (`upg-drive-in`, cost 700; `upg-wellness-center`, cost 900) remain at or near 0% M1 pick rate on the canonical `mc-balance` Medium profile because they compete for the single upgrade market slot with higher-weighted upgrades. This task raises their draw-weight (or adjusts cost/incomeBonus) to reach ≥5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones below 5% or breaking the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ladder.

## Problem statement

The upgrade-deck composition lever (MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W) added `drawWeight` values to the upgrade-deck: the four level-2 capstones and their level-1 prerequisites received weight boosts (2–3× baseline), but the remaining level-0 branching upgrades — `upg-drive-in` (Cinema, cost 700) and `upg-wellness-center` (Day Spa, cost 900) — were left with no `drawWeight` (baseline = 1). These two cards compete for the single upgrade slot in the market against weighted cards (drawWeight 2–3), so their market appearance rate is too low to achieve meaningful adoption. The previous rebalance (MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M) left them unchanged to avoid over-tuning the market composition.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the expensive-tier branching path (Cinema → Drive-In, Day Spa → Wellness Center) to be a viable investment option alongside the IMAX/Resort-Spa standard path and the multiplex/luxury-retreat capstone chain.
- **Producer / designer** — wants a balanced economy where all upgrade paths are reachable, with measurable Monte Carlo evidence.
- **Developer** — wants card-data-only changes (cost/incomeBonus/drawWeight); no engine modifications.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** Before/after Monte Carlo evidence (200 seeds, `mc-balance` prefix, 60 turns, greedy Easy/Medium/Hard) records M1 pick rate for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`.
2. **Target met.** A card-data-only change (cost/incomeBonus/drawWeight) lifts both `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center` to ≥5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`) below 5% M1 and without breaking the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ladder.
3. **Tests pass.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
4. **Fallback escalated (conditional).** If the ≥5% M1 target is unreachable by card-data-only tuning without regressing the capstones or the difficulty ladder, the shortfall is documented on this work item with before/after evidence and a follow-up work item is created to escalate (per the Constraints section).

## Constraints

- **Card data only** — no engine-rule changes. Modify `cost`, `incomeBonus`, and/or `drawWeight` in `src/card-data.csv` (or equivalent template).
- If the ≥5% M1 target is unreachable without regressing capstones or breaking the difficulty ladder, document the shortfall and escalate separately.

## Existing state

- **CSV values (current):**

  | upg-wellness-center | 900 | 250 | (unset = 1) | 0 | Day Spa |

# Migrate Main Street Renderer from Canvas to WebGL

**Related parent:** `MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38` — Create a card shader (completed, Canvas-compatible effect delivered)

## Problem statement

The game currently boots with `type: Phaser.CANVAS`, which prevents the use of Phaser 4's Filter system and custom GPU shaders. A true GPU card shader (the goal of the parent work item) requires WebGL rendering. The renderer must be migrated to WebGL so that GPU-based effects become available in production.

## Users

- **Game players** — experience GPU-accelerated card shaders with correct visual quality.
- **Developers** — can use Phaser 4's Filter/postFX pipeline for rendering effects.
- **CI/automation** — browser tests continue to run efficiently in headless environments.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **WebGL boot:** The game boots under `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL with Canvas fallback) in `main.ts` and `game-repo-scaffold.ts`, with no visual regression to existing rendering.
2. **GeometryMask migration:** All `Phaser.Display.Masks.GeometryMask` usages across Main Street and core UI are migrated to Phaser 4's `Mask` filter (or equivalent `createMask`/`addMaskShape` API). Verified across: `HelpPanel.ts`, `Overlay.ts`, `SettingsPanel.ts`, `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, `MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, `MainStreetScene.ts`, `GymCardIndexScene.ts`, and `GymOverlayUiScene.ts`.
3. **WebGL browser test:** At least one browser test project exercises WebGL rendering (e.g., a Playwright-based Chromium + SwiftShader project that forces `Phaser.WEBGL` and validates rendering correctness).
4. **Test suite passes:** Full project test suite passes with WebGL rendering.
5. **Documentation updated:** All relevant documentation reflects the WebGL migration, including comments about the `type` field and mask API changes.

## Constraints

- **CI performance:** `TestGamePool` and browser tests intentionally use Canvas for speed (~10x faster under SwiftShader). This migration must not force tests to WebGL — test factories should continue to pass `type: Phaser.CANVAS` where appropriate.
- **GeometryMask is Canvas-only in Phaser 4 RC7:** `node_modules/phaser/src/display/mask/GeometryMask.js:27` explicitly states this. Must use the Phaser 4 `Mask` class (`scene.make.mask()` or `sprite.setMask(mask)`) as the replacement.
- **WebGL blend modes:** WebGL supports only NORMAL/ADD/MULTIPLY/SCREEN blend modes. Main Street does not use exotic blend modes, so no issue expected.
- **SVG textures:** `core/src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` uses `textures.addCanvas` for SVG-derived card art. These must survive GPU re-upload in WebGL.
- **Context loss:** WebGL context loss/restoration is a new failure mode that must be considered.
- **Rendering determinism:** Visual output is not byte-identical across Canvas/WebGL/GPUs; visual regression checks may need adjustment.
- **Phaser version:** 4.0.0-rc.7 — ships only WebGL (no WebGPU). This is the intermediate step towards a future WebGL2/WebGPU backend.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/main.ts` — Change `type: Phaser.CANVAS` to `Phaser.AUTO`
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — Change `type: Phaser.CANVAS` to `Phaser.AUTO`
- `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — Replace `GeometryMask` with `Mask` filter
- `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts` — Replace `createGeometryMask()` with `createMask()`
- `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — Replace `GeometryMask` with `Mask` filter
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Replace `GeometryMask` with `Mask` filter (log mask + street map mask)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — Update any GeometryMask references
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Update type declaration for `logContentMask`
- `src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts` — Replace `createGeometryMask()` with `createMask()`
- `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` — Replace `GeometryMask` with `Mask` filter
- `core/src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` — Verify SVG textures survive WebGL
- `core/src/core-engine/TestGamePool.ts` — Confirm tests still use Canvas (no change needed)
- `core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts` — Already defaults to `Phaser.AUTO`; no change needed

## Existing state

- `createCardGame` already defaults to `Phaser.AUTO` — the Canvas restriction is applied via explicit `type: Phaser.CANVAS` overrides in `main.ts` and `game-repo-scaffold.ts`.
- `TestGamePool` and all browser tests explicitly pass `type: Phaser.CANVAS` for CI performance. This pattern should be preserved.
- GeometryMask is used in ~10+ files across Main Street, core UI, and gym scenes.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Mask API compatibility.** The Phaser 4 `Mask` filter API may differ from `GeometryMask` in how it handles dynamic shapes (scrollable content areas, street map clipping). Mitigation: verify each usage with visual testing.
- **Risk: WebGL context loss.** If the GPU driver resets, the game may need to re-initialise textures. Mitigation: implement a basic context-loss listener that logs the event; full restoration can be deferred.
- **Risk: Visual regression.** Thumbnail/visual-regression tests may produce different output under WebGL vs Canvas. Mitigation: update baseline images if acceptable.
- **Assumption: Main Street does not use exotic WebGL blend modes.** Verified — no exotic blend modes in use.
- **Assumption: SVG `addCanvas` textures work under WebGL.** Unverified — requires testing.

## Scope creep

- This work item does **not** implement the GPU card shader — it only enables the WebGL renderer. The card shader itself is tracked in `MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38` (Canvas-compatible effect delivered) and a follow-up item for the GPU version.
- WebGPU is explicitly out of scope — Phaser 4.0.0-rc.7 does not include it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should the renderer be `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL with automatic Canvas fallback) or `Phaser.WEBGL` (WebGL only, no fallback)?
  — Answer (work item description): `Phaser.AUTO` — "WebGL with Canvas fallback" stated explicitly.
- Q: Should the priority be elevated from `low` to `high` since this is a prerequisite for GPU shaders?
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): Keep `low` for now. The parent card shader item delivered a Canvas-compatible effect (Option A), so the WebGL migration is not blocking current delivery. Priority remains `low`.
- Q: What specific WebGL-only feature should the browser test exercise?
  — Answer: The test should force `Phaser.WEBGL` and verify that at least one rendering path that relies on WebGL-specific behaviour (e.g., texture filtering, mask rendering, or a simple filter) produces correct output.

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, since `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` landed, a bundled
build-time registry (the browser). There is no mechanism for hosting a pack
catalogue remotely, so publishing or updating a pack forces a rebuild and
re-release of the game. This item implements the **remote source provider** on
top of the pack-source registry abstraction (`PackSource[]` /
`PackSourceRegistry`) introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** — hosts a signed pack catalogue at a URL and
  expects packs to appear in players' Card Packs panels without rebuilding the
  game.
- **Main Street player** — experiences remote packs identically to bundled
  packs (lock → purchase → enable → deal) and continues to play offline on
  bundled packs when the remote host is unreachable.

Example user stories:

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack catalogue at a URL
> that the game verifies with a signed manifest, so I can publish or update
> packs for an installed game without rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want remote packs to appear in my Card Packs panel and behave
> exactly like bundled packs, while the game still boots and plays offline on
> bundled packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Locked design decisions (producer, 2026-10-17)

- **Q1 — Configuration: build-time config constant.** Remote source URLs are
  declared in a build-time config constant (e.g. an environment variable read
  by `vite.config.ts` / a config module), matching the bundled-source pattern.
  No runtime URL mutation in this iteration; launcher-supplied or well-known
  URLs are a possible follow-up.
- **Q2 — Integrity: signed manifests (Ed25519).** Remote manifests are signed
  (Ed25519); the game verifies the signature against a pinned public key before
  trusting any remote pack content. A manifest that fails verification is
  rejected whole (no packs from that source) with a logged warning — safe
  refusal, never a crash. Host allow-list remains as the first gate (only
  configured URLs are fetched at all).
- **Q3 — Timeout & degradation: bounded hard timeout, console-only warning.**
  A hard fetch timeout (≈3 s) bounds the boot path; on failure the game boots
  on bundled packs and logs a warning to the console. **No UI change** — no
  toast, no panel indicator. The Card Packs listing is never empty when a
  bundled pack exists.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence: bundled always wins.** When the same pack id
  appears in more than one source, the **bundled source wins**; a remote pack
  can never override bundled core content. This is implemented by keeping the
  bundled source registered *before* the remote source in the registry (the
  registry's first-wins consultation order) plus an explicit test asserting the
  precedence.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` (`createRemotePackSource`)
   that fetches a pack manifest and pack CSVs from a configured base URL via
   the loader's existing `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` transport seam and
   contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Declare remote source URLs as a build-time config
   constant (e.g. `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` or a config module), consumed when the
   default registry is built. Multiple remote sources compose additively in
   registration order, always **after** the bundled source.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Pack-id precedence is deterministic: bundled wins
   over remote (remote registered after bundled). Pack-id conflicts between two
   remote sources resolve first-wins (registration order). The core merge
   contract continues to reject duplicate card ids whole.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Remote packs are not
   automatically ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable, or serving a
   malformed manifest degrades to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never blocks boot, never blanks the listing. A bounded timeout (≈3 s) is
   applied to the manifest fetch (and per-file fetches).
6. **Trust and integrity.** Remote manifests are **Ed25519-signed**; the game
   verifies the signature against a pinned public key before trusting content.
   Failure modes: bad signature / missing signature / malformed manifest →
   reject source whole with a warning. Host allow-list: only configured URLs
   are fetched.
7. **Caching / offline.** No client-side caching of remote packs in this
   iteration — remote packs require the remote host at load time; the offline
   story is the bundled packs. Cache in `localStorage` / Cache Storage is a
   recorded follow-up.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, signed-manifest verification,
   degradation, gating, precedence and asset resolution with tests; document
   the remote-hosting contract (configuration, signing, hosting layout,
   degradation).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
   URL is fetched at runtime and its packs appear in the Card Packs panel
   alongside bundled packs.
2. **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
   lock → purchase → enable → deal flow, including save/load persistence.
3. **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
   malformed manifest, the game boots on bundled packs and logs a warning; the
   Card Packs listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists; the fetch is
   bounded by a timeout (≈3 s) so boot is never blocked.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
   header/duplicate id is rejected whole with a logged warning, without
   affecting packs from other sources.
5. **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
   with the same pack id; conflicts between remote sources resolve
   first-wins in registration order; precedence is explicit and tested.
6. **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
   missing, invalid, or not produced by the pinned key is rejected whole with a
   logged warning and no packs from that source are loaded; the failure mode is
   documented.
7. **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
   coordinated with `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (pack assets self-contained) — remote
   assets resolve through the environment-injected `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`
   seam.
8. **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
   remote configuration, the hosting contract (layout, signing), integrity and
   degradation.
9. **Testing.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes; remote
   discovery, signature verification, degradation, precedence, gating and asset
   resolution are covered by automated tests.

## Constraints

- **Reuse existing seams.** The remote source consumes the existing injectable
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports on the loader
  (`createPackSourceTransports`); no core loader changes.
- **Totality.** The remote source never throws: network failures, timeouts,
  malformed responses, signature failures, and missing files all resolve to
  `null` and the core loader degrades to bundled/static packs.
- **Additive.** The remote source is added to the existing
  `PackSourceRegistry` **after** the bundled source, without modifying bundled
  or content-directory sources.
- **Bounded timeout.** Remote fetches on the boot path are bounded (≈3 s) so
  the game never stalls waiting for a slow or hung host.
- **Signing key separation.** The pinned verification public key is a build-time
  constant; the private signing key is held by the distribution operator and is
  never shipped in the game.
- **Pack content stays licence-clean.** Remote packs must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs (documented in the hosting contract).
- **No runtime URL mutation** in this iteration (build-time config only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, signature
  verification, registration and precedence.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source configuration + transport
  wiring (consumes the `packSources` option).
- `vite.config.ts` / config module (e.g. `src/mainStreetRemotePacks.ts`) —
  build-time remote URL + pinned public key declaration.
- `src/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — remote source boot wiring.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — transport usage (should not need changes).
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, signature verification, degradation,
  precedence, asset-resolution tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline or signing tooling UI (a natural follow-up
  — the signing key/algorithm contract is defined here, tooling later).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.
- Client-side caching of remote packs for offline use (recorded follow-up).
- Runtime/launcher-supplied remote URL mutation (build-time config only).

## Related work

- **`MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`** — Make card packs available in the browser
  distribution: provides `PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry`; **blocks** this
  item (this item depends on it). Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`** — Make card-pack assets self-contained: pack art
  resolves from pack assets; remote assets must consume the
  `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` seam. Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY`** — Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import:
  parent context for the DLC channel.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; a hostile pack could
  inject arbitrary card data. *Mitigation:* Ed25519-signed manifests verified
  against a pinned public key; host allow-list; safe refusal (reject whole,
  log warning, never crash).
- **Risk — signing overhead.** Key management, signing tooling, and
  verification bugs. *Mitigation:* verification is a small, isolated,
  well-tested function; private key never ships; the public key is pinned at
  build time; signing tooling can be a follow-up (the contract is defined).
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the
  game. *Mitigation:* bounded timeout (≈3 s), non-blocking degradation,
  bundled-first registry order.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack cannot
  use it offline. *Mitigation:* explicit decision — no remote caching this
  iteration; bundled packs remain the offline story; caching recorded as a
  follow-up.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Caching, signing tooling, runtime URL mutation, and a
  pack CDN are natural follow-ups. *Mitigation:* recorded as out of scope /
  linked follow-ups, not built here.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than
  re-architecting.
- **Assumption — transport seams are adequate.** The existing
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports can serve a remote
  source without core changes.
- **Assumption — Ed25519 available.** A small Ed25519 verification
  implementation (e.g. WebCrypto `crypto.subtle`/`Ed25519`, or a tiny
  dependency) is available in the browser and test environments; the exact
  mechanism is an implementation detail the implementer records.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Configuration mechanism** (how remote source URLs are declared:
  build-time constant / launcher setting / well-known URL). — **Answer
  (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17): A — build-time config constant.**
  Matches the bundled-source pattern; simplest; runtime URL mutation is a
  recorded follow-up. Source: worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q2 — Pack-integrity model** (host allow-list / allow-list + checksum /
  signed manifests). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17):
  C — signed manifests (Ed25519).** Verification against a pinned public key;
  failure rejects the source whole with a warning. Source: worklog comment
  `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q3 — Timeout and degradation behaviour** (hard timeout + console only /
  + toast / + panel indicator). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-17): A — hard timeout (≈3 s), console warning, no UI change.**
  Source: worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence** for the same pack id across sources (bundled wins /
  last wins / first wins). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-17): A — bundled always wins.** Remote packs never override bundled
  core content; implemented via registry order + explicit test. Source:
  worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.

# Intake Brief: Add ToneForge factories for the four intentionally factory-less SFX mappings

## Problem statement

The Main Street runtime synth currently ships 12 ToneForge factories, but 16 logical SFX keys are mapped — four keys intentionally fall back to WAV because no ToneForge factory exists for them. This work item adds real ToneForge synth factories for those four keys so the synth covers all 16 mapped keys, then removes the factory-less workaround entries.

## Users

- **Game player** — expects consistent synthetic audio for all Main Street SFX rather than a mix of synth and WAV sounds.
- **Developer** — the tutorial and gameplay emit zero `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory` warnings for Main Street, keeping the console clean.

Example user stories:
- As a player, I want all Main Street SFX to use the ToneForge synth consistently, so the audio experience is unified.
- As a developer, I want no missing-factory warnings on the console when playing Main Street, so real issues stand out.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **All four new factories exist in the runtime synth module** — `income-positive-chime`, `income-negative-chime`, `income-neutral-chime`, and `success-fanfare` are present in `main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` (`factories` and `descriptors`), each producing a musically appropriate one-shot sound.
2. **All 16 mapped SFX keys play through the synth** — every key in `MAIN_STREET_TF_SFX_MAPPING` is handled by the synth player (no WAV fallback), verified by `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` (no factory-less assertion for these keys).
3. **Factory-less workaround lists are updated** — `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` and `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_FACTORY_KEYS` in `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` no longer contain the four keys (the arrays become empty).
4. **Logger and tests stay consistent** — `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` no longer references these four keys; `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` no longer asserts WAV fallback for the four keys (or asserts they play through synth instead).
5. **Full test suite passes** — all existing tests pass, including `tfFallback.test.ts` and `tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts`.

## Constraints

- New factories must follow the existing pattern in `main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` (one-shot voice, Tone synthesizer, appropriate musical character).
- Preserve the existing 12 factories unchanged.
- The four new sounds should be musically appropriate:
  - `income-positive-chime`: pleasant ascending chime (positive reinforcement)
  - `income-negative-chime`: descending/flat tone (negative feedback, not alarming)
  - `income-neutral-chime`: single soft note (neutral indication)
  - `success-fanfare`: short celebratory multi-note fanfare
- No changes to the engine/core beyond the runtime synth module.
- No new external dependencies.

## Existing state

- `core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` — ships 12 factories with `descriptors` and `factories` exports; uses helper functions `oneShotVoice()`, `movementVoice()`, `ambienceVoice()`, etc.
- `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` — maps 16 keys; 4 intentionally factory-less (tracked in `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS`).
- `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` — suppresses missing-factory warnings for the 4 factory-less keys.
- `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` — asserts that factory-less keys fall back to WAV.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` — asserts no console warnings for the factory-less keys.

## Key Files

- `core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` — Add 4 new factory entries and descriptor entries.
- `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` — Remove 4 keys from `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS`.
- `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` — No code change needed (it derives `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` from the mapping dynamically), but verify.
- `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` — Remove/assertion update for the four keys (they should now play via synth).
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` — Update any assertions that expect WAV fallback for the four keys.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUU9QYQE006NLEZ** — Activate ToneForge runtime synth: loader diagnostics + scene wiring (completed)
- **MS-0MV26MOWT004ZCQC** — Console noise when running the tutorial (completed) — silenced per-play warnings for factory-less keys
- **CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76** — Engine contract: WAV fallback for missing factories
- **CG-0MUTU0MFE0077H0F** — Engine ToneForge foundation

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the four sounds should be synthesized (not WAV) — consistent with the synth-first approach of the runtime module.
- **Assumption:** each sound is a short one-shot (≤ 1 second) — consistent with the existing factory pattern.
- **Risk:** musical quality of synthesized sounds is subjective. Mitigation: keep sounds simple and consistent with the existing 12 factories.
- **Risk:** the runtime synth module is a static ESM file that gets bundled — adding factories should not change bundle size meaningfully.
- **Scope-creep:** adding more factory-less keys from other games is out of scope; this item covers only the four Main Street keys.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context plus extensive repository evidence determined scope and approach.

- Q: "What musical character should each of the four sounds have?" — Answer (inferred from names): positive-chime (pleasant ascending), negative-chime (descending/flat but not alarming), neutral-chime (soft single note), success-fanfare (celebratory multi-note). Source: work-item title + naming convention.
- Q: "Should the logger file be updated manually?" — Answer: no manual change needed — `tfLogger.ts` derives `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` dynamically from `sfx-tf-mapping.ts`, so removing from the mapping list automatically removes them from the logger's suppression set. Source: repo evidence, `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` lines 35-42.

# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).
  - **No additional stats** beyond the five listed (producer Q4 = "No").
  - **Layout = add a third column** to the Game Over overlay (producer Q5),
    rather than a separate full-page stats screen.
- Game engine is **Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`**; overlay rendering lives in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`.
- External chart library integration with the Phaser canvas must not regress
  headless/Monte-Carlo runs or replay mode (chart module is skipped there).
- CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD
  pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- **Game Over overlay:** `showGameOverOverlay()` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — two columns (**Game State** /
  **Summary**) with a top band (title + end-reason headline) and the
  Play Again / Menu controls anchored at the panel bottom (panel is 900 px
  wide, laid out by `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap`). The pure, Phaser-free
  content model is `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`
  (`buildGameOverPlayerRows`, `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`,
  `formatEndReason`).
- **Current-turn snapshot:** `state.weekStartCoins` / `weekStartRep` /
  `weekStartScore` are set in `executeWeekStart`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`) and serialised in
  `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The per-turn net row
  (`appendTurnNetRow`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) derives the
  turn's deltas from that snapshot and logs
  `Turn <n> net: <deltas> (score: <delta>)`.
- **Ledger history:** `EconomyLedger.getHistory()`
  (`core/src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, imported as
  `@rule-engine/EconomyLedger`) records *every mutation*, is **not
  serialised**, and is **not per-turn** — unsuitable as-is for the graphs.
- **Counts available at turn end:** businesses = non-null entries in
  `state.streetGrid`; staff = `state.staffCards.length`; cash/reputation =
  `state.resourceBank`; score = `state.finalScore`.
- **Precedent:** the Monte Carlo harness already captures a per-turn series
  (`economyHistory: [{ turn, coins, reputation, score }]`) in
  `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` for balance analytics — a useful shape to
  mirror.
- **Save/load:** `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, with legacy fallbacks for absent
  fields.

## Desired change

1. **State.** Add a `TurnStatSnapshot` interface (`turn`, `coins`,
   `reputation`, `score`, `profit`, `businesses`, `staff`) and
   `turnStatsHistory: TurnStatSnapshot[]` to `MainStreetState`; initialise it
   to `[]` in `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState`.
2. **Capture.** Record one snapshot at the end of each completed turn —
   covering the **deferred** path (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, after deltas
   are applied) and the **legacy** path — so the turn's net profit is computed
   against `weekStartCoins` exactly like `appendTurnNetRow`. Guard against
   double-recording when the two paths overlap (e.g. keyed by `turn`).
3. **Persistence.** Serialise `turnStatsHistory`; on load, default to `[]`
   for legacy saves.
4. **Model.** Extend `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` with a pure
   series builder (e.g. `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)`) returning the five
   requested series plus the final "cash at end of turn" value.
5. **Render.** Add a **third column** to `showGameOverOverlay()` rendering the
   graphs via the chosen external charting library (encapsulated in a small
   helper module so the model stays Phaser-free and testable), and add the
   **Cash at end of turn** line plus a link to the stats column on the Summary
   column. Recompute `panelW` / column widths / `panelH` so all three columns
   fit the 1280×720 viewport.
6. **Guardrails.** Skip chart construction in `scene.replayMode` / headless
   mode; keep the pure model testable without booting Phaser or the chart
   library.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory`
  to `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Initialise `turnStatsHistory: []` for
  single-player and competitive setups.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Record the per-turn snapshot on both
  closing paths (reuse the `weekStartCoins`/`appendTurnNetRow` pattern).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — Serialise/restore `turnStatsHistory`
  with a legacy `[]` fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — New pure series builder
  (`buildGameOverStatSeries`) + final cash-at-end-of-turn value.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Third column rendering + Summary
  cash line + link; widen/rebalance the panel layout.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **New** thin wrapper around the
  external charting library (skipped in replay/headless).
- `package.json` — Add the charting-library dependency.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats.test.ts` — **New** unit tests (capture,
  round-trip, legacy fallback, series model).
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Third-column and cash-line
  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —
  Document per-turn history and the end-of-game stats column.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed) — the
  epic that built the current Game Over overlay.
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed) — the
  layout this item extends to a third column.
- **MS-0MUWE6MA30038RGY** – Game-over summary test harness (completed) — the
  fixture/helper pattern to reuse for tests.
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat
  (completed) — introduced the per-seat Game Over breakdown.
- **MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7** – Storyline coverage analytics in Monte Carlo
  harness (open) — consumes a per-turn economy series, the same shape this
  item persists.
- **Related docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log —
  Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net, § Win conditions),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.
- Automated find-related report appended below (if produced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — external chart library vs Phaser canvas.** Chart.js needs a canvas
  context; overlaying it on the Phaser canvas and keeping it out of
  headless/replay runs needs care. *Mitigation:* isolate the library behind
  `MainStreetStatsChart.ts`, lazy-load/skip in replay/headless, verify bundle
  size.
- **Risk — deferred vs legacy capture paths** could double-record or miss the
  final turn. *Mitigation:* record keyed by `turn` in the shared closing tail,
  with targeted unit tests for both paths.
- **Risk — save/load compatibility.** *Mitigation:* legacy fallback to `[]`,
  with a round-trip + legacy test.
- **Risk — three-column overflow at 1280×720.** *Mitigation:* recompute panel
  width/height and add a browser fit assertion.
- **Assumption — competitive-mode series scope.** In single-player the five
  series describe the run's economy. In competitive mode the shared
  `resourceBank` is seat-scoped during a turn; this brief assumes the graphs
  show the **human seat's** trajectory. *Open question, recorded in the
  Appendix* — the producer may instead want every seat as a separate series.
- **Assumption — "link to a more detailed screen" is satisfied by the third
  column**, per producer Q5; no separate scene is added.
- **Scope-creep risk:** additional stats or chart types beyond the five listed
  (producer Q4 = none) must be raised as separate work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Correct project?** This item was created in ContextHub (the Worklog
  CLI tool) but describes a Main Street game screen.
  - **Answer (producer): `tce-main-street`.** Source: interactive reply,
    2026-10-16. *Action:* item relocated — created as MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV in
    `tce-main-street`; the mis-filed WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02 was closed as a
    relocated duplicate.

- **Q2 — Per-turn history tracking.** The save holds only the current-turn
  `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score` snapshot; a full per-turn history must be added
  unless the save already carries one.
  - (A) Add per-turn history tracking, reusing the snapshot mechanism.
    **Recommended.**
  - (B) Use only static current values (no historical graphs).
  - **Answer (producer):** "Doesn't the save game have that snapshot? If not A
    otherwise reuse that mechanism." *Research:* inspected
    `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — the save persists only the **current**
    `weekStart*` snapshot, not a per-turn series; the `EconomyLedger` history
    is per-mutation and not serialised. Therefore **Option A** applies, reusing
    the `weekStart*` snapshot pattern and persisting a new series. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q3 — Chart/graph approach.**
  - (A) Phaser-based line/bar charts (custom `Graphics`). **Recommended** at
    the time of asking (no new dependency).
  - (B) External charting library (e.g. Chart.js).
  - (C) SVG line plots rendered as Phaser textures.
  - **Answer (producer): B** — use an external charting library (overrode the
    recommendation). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q4 — Additional stats?** Beyond profit/turn, businesses, cash, staff and
  reputation at end of turn.
  - **Answer (producer): No.** Only the five listed stats. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q5 — Summary-screen placement / detailed screen.** "Place the cash at end
  of turn on the summary screen and add a link to a more detailed screen" — is
  the Summary column the right place, with a button to a full-page graph view?
  - **Answer (producer): Add a third column.** The detailed graphs live in a
    third column of the Game Over overlay rather than a separate screen.
    Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope).** In competitive mode,
  should the graphs plot (i) only the human seat's trajectory, or (ii) every
  seat as a separate series? *Working assumption: (i) human seat only.* Noted
  for producer confirmation during review; not blocking.

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed)

# Intake brief: Port the Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) guard to sibling game repos' `vite.config.ts`

## Problem statement

The core scaffold template (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA) emits `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` (covering `**/.worklog/**` and the dev-output trees), and `tce-main-street` and `tce-the-rising` already carry the block — but 8 sibling game repos' checked-in `vite.config.ts` still lack it: `AI_Hell`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go`. When any of these repos accumulates `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (AI_Hell already has 9 + a nested `ToneForge` checkout), the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively walks them and exhausts the host `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` budget — `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` — crashing the dev server and breaking test runs (the exact failure mode fixed in the parent item MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY).

## Users

- **Developers/agents working in any Tableau-Card-Engine game repo** (tce-\*) — must be able to run `npm run dev` and `npm test` from the main checkout once worktrees exist without tripping the host watcher limit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer in tce-blackjack, I want my dev server to ignore `.worklog/worktrees/**` so a recursive watch never exhausts inotify (ENOSPC)."
- **AI_Hell maintainers** (in scope — Q1 answered) — same failure mode is already active (9 worktree checkouts).
  - *User story:* "As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same watcher guard, so my `vite` dev server survives `.worklog/worktrees/**` growth."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in sibling repos must not fail with ENOSPC.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Watcher guard present in every in-scope repo's checked-in config.** The 7 tce-\* repos each import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin` and set `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` with the template's explanatory comment (wording as in CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA / `tce-the-rising`). AI_Hell (if in scope) sets `watch.ignored` from a locally defined constant covering `**/.worklog/**` (plus its dev-output trees). ## Summary

Generalise the `storylines:graph` conventions into a dev-only diagram generator
(`src/scripts/card-diagrams.ts` + `card-diagrams-cli.ts`, npm script
`docs:diagrams`) with `--diagram --format --out --check`, and deliver the

   `--diagram <synergies|staff|upgrades|community-spaces|all>` (default `all`),
   `--format mermaid|json` (default `mermaid`), `--out <path>`,
   `--check` (drift guard: exit `1` on drift, `0` when up to date; stderr
   prints a regenerate command on drift/missing artefact).

   multi-synergy edges — `biz-cafe` → Food + Culture, `cs-public-art` →
